Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 
Author: Pradeep Singh Yerur Bench: Pradeep Singh Yerur  -1-  NC: 2024:KHC:16244  MFA No. 413 of 2020  IN THE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA AT BENGALURU  DATED THIS THE 23RD DAY OF APRIL, 2024  BEFORE  THE HON'BLE MR JUSTICE PRADEEP SINGH YERUR  MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL NO.413 OF 2020 (MV-I)
 BETWEEN:
 SRI SURESH  S/O.SHANMUKHA SHETTY  AGED ABOUT 39 YEARS  R/AT WEAVERS COLONY  BEHIND RAM MANDIR  NELAMANGALA TALUK  BENGALURU RURAL DISTRICT-562 123  ...APPELLANT  (BY SRI SURESH M. LATUR, ADVOCATE)
 AND:
 1. SRI SENTHIL B.
 S/O.VAJRAVEL  R/AT NO.525, N.NO.4/53  SANJEEVAPURAM  THIYOPPANAHLLI POST Digitally signed PONNAGARAM by GAVRIBIDANUR DHARMAPURI SUBRAMANYA GUPTA TAMIL NADU-636 701 SREENATH Location: HIGH 2 .
COURT OF THE MANAGER KARNATAKA NATIONAL INSURANCE  COMPANY LIMITED  SUBBARAM COMPLEX  M.G.ROAD  BENGALURU-560 010  ...RESPONDENTS  (BY SRI E.I.SANMATHI, ADVOCATE FOR R-2;
Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96044356/ 
1  NOTICE TO R-1 IS DISPENSED V/ O.DATED 21.03.2022 ) 
 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO MODIFY THE  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:16244  MFA No. 413 of 2020 JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 08.11.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.6525/2016 BY C/c XIII ADDITIONAL JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES AND MACT, BENGALURU.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT This appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 08.11.2019 passed in MVC.No.6525/2016 by the Court of C/c XIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes and Member, MACT, Bengaluru (for short 'the tribunal'). The appeal is preferred on the premise of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal. 
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal. 
3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
On 21.08.2016 at about 5.15 p.m., the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-04-EP-9484 on Bagalur to Dommasandra.
When he reached near Bagalur-Sarjapur main road, Rajiv Gandhi Nagar, a Bolero vehicle bearing NC: 2024:KHC:16244 registration No.TN-29-AL-3486 which was proceeding in front of the said motor cycle with high speed in a rash and negligent manner suddenly applied brake and took right side of the road. As a result, the rider of the said motor cycle lost control and hit the said Bolero. Due to the sudden impact,
the claimant fell down and sustained injuries all over his body. He was immediately shifted to Hosur Government Hospital and later, he was shifted to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru, where he spent huge amount towards treatment. Due to the injuries sustained and disability suffered, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation. 
3.1 On service of notice, respondent No.1 was placed ex parte. Respondent No.2 filed written statement denying the claim of the claimant including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. Bolero vehicle. It is also pleaded that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of NC: 2024:KHC:16244 the motor cycle and sought for dismissal of the claim Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96044356/
2 petition.
3.2 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration. 
3.3 In order to substantiate the issue and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1, the Doctor as PW.2 and two other witnesses as PWs.3 and 4 and got marked documents from Exs.P1 to P16(a). On the contrary, respondent No.2 neither examined a witness nor got marked any documents. 
3.4 On the basis of material evidence produced by the parties, the tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.3,94,420/- with interest @ 7% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the compensation within two months. The tribunal also fastened 20%
contributory negligence as against the rider of the motor cycle i.e. the claimant and remaining 80% as against the owner of Bolero vehicle i.e. respondent No.1. 
NC: 2024:KHC:16244 3.5 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation. 
4. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the appellant that the income and disability of the appellant assessed by the Tribunal are on the lower side and the compensation awarded under different heads is not in accordance with the material on record. Learned counsel further contends that in view of disability to an extent of 64% to the right lower limb, future prospects requires to be awarded as the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and he is unable to do work as he was doing prior to occurrence of the accident. It is further contention of learned counsel that the accident did not occur due to triple riding of the motorcycle without wearing of helmets and infact, it may be violation of law, but such violation by itself cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence and therefore he seeks to set aside the finding of the Tribunal insofar as fixing 20% NC:
2024:KHC:16244 contributory negligence on the claimant. On these grounds, he seeks to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation. 
5. In support of his contentions, learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon the following judgments:
i) Meera Devi and another -vs- Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others - 2014 ACJ ii) Kiran -vs- Sajja Singh and others - 2014 ACJ iii) Mohammed Siddique and another -vs- National Insurance Co. Ltd. and others - 2020 ACJ 751 iv) Raghavendra - Kengaiah and others - 2016 ACJ 1094 Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96044356/
3 v) New India Assurance Co. Ltd. -vs- Durgappa and others - 2017 ACJ 2600 vi) M.S. Lokesh -vs- Achappa and another - 2017 ACJ 1065 NC: 2024:KHC:16244 vii) Pappu Deo Yadau -vs- Naresh Kumar and others - 2020 ACJ 2695 viii) Gopalappa -vs- Kandaluru Shankar Reddy and another - 2022 ACJ 1427 6. Per contra, learned counsel representing the insurance company contends that there is no error,
illegality or perversity in the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal. He further contends that the Tribunal awarded just and reasonable compensation under all heads, in accordance with the material evidence, both oral and documentary and the same does not call for interference. It is also contention of learned counsel that the accident occurred due to triple riding of the motorcycle without wearing of helmets and therefore the Tribunal rightly fastened 20%
contributory negligence against the claimant. On these grounds, learned counsel sought for dismissal of the appeal. 
7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material on record, it is seen that FIR NC: 2024:KHC:16244 has been registered against driver of the offending vehicle i.e, Bolero for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and same has not been challenged or controverted. The occurrence of accident, involvement of vehicle, injuries sustained by the claimant and the accident occurred due to negligence of driver of the offending vehicle are established by the evidence adduced and the documents produced as per Ex.P1 to Ex.16(a). 
Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence against driver of the Bolero vehicle. 
8. Now coming to the question of age, avocation, income and disability suffered by the claimant, it is seen that the claimant was aged 33 years as on the date of accident and the appropriate multiplier would be '16', which is rightly applied by the tribunal and the same does not call for interference. 
Though the claimant pleaded that he was working as a weaver earning Rs.15,000/- per month, no material is placed before the Court with regard to the same and proof of income. In the absence of the NC: 2024:KHC:16244 same, the Tribunal has taken the income of the claimant to be Rs.7,000/-
per month, whereas the Legal Services Authority chart prescribes the notional income of Rs.9,500/-
per month for the accident of the year 2016. Accordingly, the same is taken as income for computation in the present case as against Rs.7,000/- taken by the Tribunal. 
9. The doctor has been examined as PW.2. He opined disability to an extent of 64.14% to right lower limb and 32% to whole body. The Tribunal taken the whole body disability to be 18%. I am in agreement with learned counsel for the appellant that the disability assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side. There is no contra material placed on record and cogent evidence adduced by the Insurance Company by producing second opinion or any other medical opinion to contradict the statement of the doctor/PW.2. Even one-third portion of particular limb disability is taken as a whole body disability, it would come to 21%. On appreciation of - 10 - Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96044356/
4 NC: 2024:KHC:16244 evidence of the doctor and considering the age, avocation and nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, I deem it appropriate to assess the functional disability of the claimant to be 21%. 
10. I am in agreement with learned counsel for the claimant that considering the fact that there is a disability of 64% to the right lower limb and 32% to whole body, future prospects requires to be awarded in this case. The claimant was working as a weaver earning Rs.15,000/- per month prior to the accident. Due to the accident, the claimant suffered permanent disability and he would not be able to sit, squat to perform his regular day to day activities of earning as opined by the doctor. 
Considering the disability suffered by the claimant, this Court deems it appropriate to add 40% of income towards future prospects while computing compensation under the head of loss of future earnings. 
11. In view of the above, loss of future earnings would be Rs.5,36,256/- {[Rs.9,500 + 3800 (40%)] x 12 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 x 16 x 21%} as against Rs.2,41,920/- awarded by the Tribunal. 
12. The tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering. However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.20,000/-. In all, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head. 
13. The tribunal awarded Rs.8,000/- towards food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
14. The Tribunal awarded Rs.33,500/- towards medical expenses on the basis of the actual bills produced by the claimant, which does not call for interference. 
15. The Tribunal awarded Rs.21,000/- towards loss of income during the period of treatment, which is on the lower side. Considering the magnitude of injuries suffered by the claimant, atleast three months is required to recuperate and get back to normal day to day activities. In view of this Court enhancing the income to Rs.9,500/-
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 per month, Rs.28,500/- (Rs.9,500/- x 3) is awarded under this head. 
16. The tribunal awarded Rs.35,000/- towards loss of amenities. However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.10,000/-. In all, Rs.45,000/- is awarded under this head. 
Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96044356/
5 17. The tribunal awarded Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses, which does not call for interference and the same is retained. 
18. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,26,256/- as against Rs.3,94,420/- awarded by the Tribunal, as mentioned in the table below: 
Sl. Head of compensation Amount of No. compensation  awarded  1 Loss of future earnings Rs. 5,36,256-00  2 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000-00  3 Food, nourishment, Rs. 8,000-00  conveyance and attendant  charges  - 13 -  NC: 2024:KHC:16244  4 Medical expenses Rs. 33,500-00  5 Loss of income during the Rs. 28,500-00  period of treatment  6 Loss of amenities Rs. 45,000-00  7 Future medical expenses Rs. 25,000-00  Total Rs. 7,26,256-00 19. Coming to the question of Tribunal fixing 20% contributory negligence against the claimant, it is to be borne in mind that the claimant was not the rider of the motorcycle, but he was the pillion rider. The finding arrived at by the Tribunal is not acceptable and same is erroneous and liable to be set aside. Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the rider of a two wheeler, not to carry more than one person on the motorcycle and Section 194-C prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motorcycle riders and pillion riders. The fact that the claimant was a pillion rider on a motorcycle alongwith the rider and one more person is not in dispute. The triple riding of the motorcycle by the rider without wearing of helmets may be violation of law,
- 14 - Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96044356/
6 NC: 2024:KHC:16244 but such violation by itself, without anything more specifically attributing to have contributed to the occurrence of accident, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence,
unless it is established that triple riding contributed to the accident. In the present case, there is no cogent evidence of filing FIR or criminal prosecution against rider of the motorcycle. Considering all these aspects, fastening 20% contributory negligence against claimant is perverse and same is set aside and the entire negligence is saddled on the driver of the Bolero vehicle. As the policy was in force as on the date of occurrence of the accident, the 2nd respondent/insurer shall deposit the entire compensation. 
20. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part;
ii) The impugned Judgment & Award dated 8th November 2019 passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.6325/2016, is modified.
iii) The appellant/claimant would be entitled to compensation of Rs.7,26,256/-
(Rupees seven - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 lakhs twenty-six thousand two hundred and fifty-six only) as against Rs.3,94,420/- awarded by the Tribunal.
iv) The impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal insofar as fixing 20% contributory negligence against the claimant, is hereby set aside.
v) The interest awarded by the tribunal at the rate of 7% per annum on the compensation amount of Rs.3,15,500/- is left undisturbed. However, future medical expenses shall not carry interest. 
vi) The enhanced compensation alongwith interest at 6% per annum shall be deposited by the respondent no.2/insurer within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment. 
vii) The compensation amount shall be released in favour of the appellant-claimant as per the terms of the tribunal upon proper identification. 
viii) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the tribunal shall stand intact. 
- 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 Sri Suresh vs Sri Senthil B on 23 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96044356/
7 ix) Registry is directed to transmit the original records, if any to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith. 
Sd/-

There is no contra material placed on record and cogent evidence adduced by the Insurance Company by producing second opinion or any other medical opinion to contradict the statement of the doctor/PW.2.

summary.decision:
11. In view of the above, loss of future earnings would be Rs.5,36,256/- {[Rs.9,500 + 3800 (40%)] x 12 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 x 16 x 21%} as against Rs.2,41,920/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. The tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.20,000/-.
In all, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
13. The tribunal awarded Rs.8,000/- towards food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
14.
In view of this Court enhancing the income to Rs.9,500/-
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 per month, Rs.28,500/- (Rs.9,500/- x 3) is awarded under this head.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.10,000/-.
In all, Rs.45,000/- is awarded under this head.
Considering all these aspects, fastening 20% contributory negligence against claimant is perverse and same is set aside and the entire negligence is saddled on the driver of the Bolero vehicle.
As the policy was in force as on the date of occurrence of the accident, the 2nd respondent/insurer shall deposit the entire compensation.
20. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part;
ii) The impugned Judgment & Award dated 8th November 2019 passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.6325/2016, is modified.
iii) The appellant/claimant would be entitled to compensation of Rs.7,26,256/-
(Rupees seven - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 lakhs twenty-six thousand two hundred and fifty-six only) as against Rs.3,94,420/- awarded by the Tribunal.
iv) The impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal insofar as fixing 20% contributory negligence against the claimant, is hereby set aside.
v) The interest awarded by the tribunal at the rate of 7% per annum on the compensation amount of Rs.3,15,500/- is left undisturbed.
However, future medical expenses shall not carry interest.

vi) The enhanced compensation alongwith interest at 6% per annum shall be deposited by the respondent no.2/insurer within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.

vii) The compensation amount shall be released in favour of the appellant-claimant as per the terms of the tribunal upon proper identification.

viii) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the tribunal shall stand intact.
ix) Registry is directed to transmit the original records, if any to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.
